semantics: Test-body Effect.run* sites that stay, per AGENTS.md ("Effect-native tests"): a test body that executes an Effect program uses it.effect with Effect.gen + yield*, never await Effect.runPromise(...); runPromise stays legitimate in hooks and in non-test helpers. Owned by scripts/check-effect-test-runs.mjs, which counts calls named runPromise, runPromiseExit, runFork or runCallback -- on Effect, on any locally bound runtime (testRuntime(), runtime, services.runtime), or bare -- whose innermost enclosing boundary is a test callback, including a curried factory's callback (it.each(cases)(name, body)); runSync is deliberately NOT counted, because a synchronous body has nothing to yield* and the rule names the Promise-returning runs. Hook, helper, describe and double (mock factory, vi.waitFor) boundaries do not count, and a bare name the file declares itself is the file's own helper, not a run. Every entry is a per-file allowlist of exact shrink-only counts with the reason that site stays: a count that rose, a site in a file absent from the list, a count that fell (stale headroom), or a listed file that no longer exists fails. `--update` lowers counts and drops zeroed entries but never adds a file, and it fails rather than guesses when a file has no recorded reason. The production counterpart is the 'Effect.run*' row of scripts/check-effect-migration-ratchet.mjs, whose scan roots exclude src/test-kernel.

src/test-kernel/cli/WorkflowInputsLifecy.reason: The body forks the subject's own body-local ManagedRuntime and asserts that the lifecycle shutdown disposes that runtime (Fiber.await expects a Failure for exactly that reason), so the receiver is the assertion subject and cannot disappear; the suite is otherwise it.live + Effect.gen.

src/test-kernel/desktop/JsonStore.vitest.reason: The Effect run belongs to the module under test: the body builds an esbuild bundle and imports it, so `bundledEffect` is that bundle's own Effect instance, which the test's tester cannot run; JsonStore is also on the 1.0 retirement boundary.

src/test-kernel/platform/processRuntime..reason: These are runs of the subject: the suite tests the process runtime's own fork-failure reporting, so `runtime.runFork` is the asserted behaviour and not the test executing its program; the bodies are already it.live + Effect.gen.
